gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured brightness for any 16-inch 2560x1600 portable screen: named reviewers put the ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG at 417 to 479 nits against a 500-nit claim, the Arzopa Z1RC at 415.7 nits against 500 and the UPERFECT UPlays C2 at 238 nits against 400, while the Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro's 350 nits has no independent measurement.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's Mac roundup (updated Nov 25, 2026), PCWorld's roundup (Jun 26, 2026) and TechRadar's roundup (Nov 20, 2026). Macworld lists the Duex Float 2 Pro with unattributed 'up to 350 nits', 2.9 lb and 65 W and gives no measured brightness or power draw for it. PCWorld gives measured brightness only for other sizes or panels (Arzopa Z1FC 337 nits, ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED 457 nits) and names none of the 16-inch 2560x1600 candidates. TechRadar's roundup loaded only as far as its first pick and a photo caption for the Arzopa Z3FC, with no figures. Limits: the RTINGS picks page returned navigation only and seattlepi.com was blocked, so I could not check either for these figures; that is why this is 2, not 3.
decides: It confirms the Duex Float 2 Pro as the pick on the 16:10 / 120 Hz match, but it changes how the brightness tiebreak can be written. Brightness cannot be ranked on makers' claims: the UPERFECT C2's 400-nit claim sits above the Float's 350, yet the only named measurement of it is 238 nits (Parkablogs, 2023 unit). The Float's 350 nits must be labelled as Mobile Pixels' figure, since the three reviews I opened (Macworld roundup, Mighty Gadget, Homecrux) only repeat it. The only 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz screen with a named measurement above 400 nits is the ASUS MB16QHG, and PC Pro found it limited to 60% brightness on a single USB-C cable, which is how a MacBook Pro shopper would run it. The Arzopa Z1RC is the best-measured of the group (415.7 nits, 11.0 W) but is 60 Hz, so it stays the budget row, not the match.
